title: Greek Salad
subtitle: tomato, cucumber, feta, olives, and olive oil
excerpt: A proper Greek salad -- known in Greece as horiatiki, or village salad -- has no lettuce. It is chunky pieces of tomato, cucumber, onion, and pepper with a block of feta on top and good olives. Olive oil and dried oregano are the only dressing.
sourceNotes: Horiatiki, the Greek village salad, is the everyday salad of Greece. It requires no cooking and depends on the quality of the ingredients -- ripe tomatoes, good feta, and fruity olive oil.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Prepare the vegetables up to 1 hour ahead. Add the feta and dressing just before serving.

content.text: Use the ripest tomatoes you can find. Out of season, let tomatoes sit at room temperature for a day before using. Never refrigerate them.
Arrange the tomato, cucumber, onion, and pepper in a bowl or on a platter.
Place the block of feta on top. Scatter over the olives.
Drizzle generously with olive oil. Squeeze over lemon juice if using. Sprinkle with dried oregano and flaked salt.
Serve immediately with bread to mop up the juices.

items.fix: Salt the tomato and cucumber lightly 10 minutes before assembling. Drain off the liquid.

items.cause: Some feta brands are heavily brined
items.fix: Rinse the feta briefly under cold water and pat dry before using.

content.text: Horiatiki is the everyday salad of Greek home cooking. It is eaten across the country in summer, when tomatoes are at their peak. The word means village salad, a reference to its simple, rural origins. In Greece it is served as a side dish or a shared starter, never as a course on its own. The best versions are made from the simplest ingredients.
